findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, Nov 2029): APH failed because FY2026's 29.5% operating margin and +60% sales were the top of a hyperscaler AI capex wave, not a new base. IT datacom (43% of Q2 2026 sales, virtually all of its growth AI) rolled over in 2027-28 as hyperscalers digested capacity and the next NVIDIA rack generation moved more of the in-rack interconnect to PCB/co-packaged optics, while a second source took share. Volume and margin fell together (operating margin back toward the 19-21% of 2020-2024), and the leverage taken for CommScope (debt 17.9B, goodwill 17.7B above equity 17.1B, CommScope earning about 6% on its 10.5B price) turned a cyclical dip into a de-rating: growth kept coming only from full-price acquisitions at about a 15% return. The P/E fell from about 22x forward to the mid-teens on lower EPS, as in the bear (about 43-47$). What would have shown it early: book-to-bill below 1.0 in Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 (it was 1.19 in Q3); sequential sales down in any 2027 quarter; IT datacom organic growth y/y under 10% by Q2 2027; operating margin under 27% in H1 2027 without a tariff explanation; hyperscaler capex guides for 2027 flat or down; NVIDIA Kyber/Rubin Ultra disclosures that cut copper cable content per rack.
findings.where: position/core.json events + falsifiers (all scenarios); companies/APH/out/table_he.md key-risk row
findings.fix: Keep as the counter-thesis next to the result; add the early-warning metrics missing from the falsifiers (sequential sales decline in any 2027 quarter, H1 2027 operating margin < 0.27, hyperscaler 2027 capex guide) to the bear's falsifier list in position/core.json.

findings.finding: Base growth sits at the optimistic edge, and the base falsifiers do not test the base. The 23% FY2027 growth (position/core.json drivers.growth_anchor.base) rests on a Q4 2026 of about 11.5B: the Q4 guide midpoint 10.4B times the full mean beat ratio 1.11. That is +12% q/q after Q3's 10.23B, when management's own guide is only +1-2% q/q. With Q4 at the guide and +1% a quarter in 2027 (the base event's own wording), FY2027 is about 42.6B, i.e. +15%, not +23%. The falsifiers then cannot refute the base: 'revenue Q4 2026 below 10.3B' fires only below the low end of the guide (the base assumes about 11.5B), and 'revenue FY2027 below 42B' sits about 10% under the base's implied ~46.5B (core 37B guide x track record -> ~38B x 1.23). A Q4 of 10.5B and an FY2027 of 43B would clearly refute the base and trigger neither.
findings.where: position/core.json drivers.growth_anchor (base) and scenario falsifiers for base; position/coherence.md base
findings.fix: Either take a base Q4 nearer the guide (track-record ratio at the median of the recent, smaller beats, not the mean) and lower base FY2027 growth accordingly, or keep 23% and set the base falsifiers at the base's own numbers: revenue Q4 2026 below about 11.0B by 2027-02-15 and revenue FY2027 below about 44.5B by 2028-02-28.

findings.finding: Base path return on capital is higher than the base's own DCF economics and is drawn from peak-margin data. company_path base uses roic 0.25 (justified_high), taken from TTM after-tax operating return of 23-29% on all capital at the 29.5% peak operating margin, while the base's own drivers bring the margin down to 26% and the DCF uses terminal_roic 0.20 (bull 0.32 vs 0.245; bear 0.15 vs 0.164). The two halves of the table therefore rest on different economics for the same scenario; at a 26% margin the TTM return on the same capital would be about 20-25%, not 23-29%.
findings.where: position/path.json company_path.scenarios.base.roic (and bull.roic); position/core.json drivers.terminal_roic; casefile.json company_path.scenarios.<s>.economics
findings.fix: Set the path roic per scenario to the scenario's own margin economics (base about 0.20-0.22, matching terminal_roic, or justify the gap with evidence), and rerun ticker-value; label base 'justified_high' only if the 25% survives at the 26% margin.

findings.finding: Base multiples far above the company's own history. The base path starts at a 39.1x forward P/E (143$ at year 0, 28.7x at year 5) against APH's own 2021-2025 median of 25.1x and a 21.7x forward P/E at today's 79.47$ on the base FY2027 EPS of 3.66$. The base also carries growth of about 9-19% a year through FY2033 and a terminal growth of 4.5-5.0% against a terminal cost of equity of 8.1%; the table's own outside-view row says only about 3% of companies this size sustained the base's growth. The 'cheap by about 42%' and '+154% in 5 years' readings depend on this, so the base is not shown as the most likely path.
findings.where: companies/APH/out/table_he.md (fair value, 5-year potential, yearly base row); casefile.json company_path.scenarios.base.economics.multiple_path; val.case assumptions growth_fade, terminal_base
findings.fix: State next to the result that the base multiple is about 1.5x the company's own median and that the discount rests on a long high-growth fade plus a terminal growth near the risk-free rate; consider a faster base fade (excess growth halving in 2 years rather than 3) given the AI-cycle concentration, and show the value at the own-history multiple (about 25x on base EPS: about 92$ at year 0) as a sensitivity row behind the scenes.

findings.finding: The bull is a peak-quarter x 4 at a 71x multiple. Bull roic 0.32 comes from the record Q3 2026 annualized, and the path starts at 71.2x forward (287.6$ at year 0, +292% in year 1, +431% in 5 years), almost three times the own-history median of 25.1x. It is labelled peak, which is honest, but a +292% one-year price is not a usable 'what must happen' case for the owner; it mostly reflects the economics formula applied to 32% returns for 16 years.
findings.where: position/path.json company_path.scenarios.bull; companies/APH/out/table_he.md yearly bull row and 5-year potential row
findings.fix: Cap the bull path roic at a level the company has shown over a full year (the TTM 23-29% on all capital) or cap the multiple at the company's own historical high, and rerun; otherwise add a line under the table that the bull prices rest on one record quarter.

findings.finding: Business model misrouted on a keyword. The card classifies APH as capital_intensive_infrastructure because its industry text contains 'cable' (case archetype 'infrastructure'), while its signature (gross margin 36.9%, capex about 3.9% of revenue, connectors/sensors/antennas manufacturer, SIC 3678) is hardware manufacturing / electronic components; the sector match 'electronic components -> hardware_manufacturing' was discarded only because the industry label was 'more specific'. The archetype can change the fade, reinvestment and multiple rules applied.
findings.fix: Override business_model.primary to hardware_manufacturing (electronic components) with the 10-K Item 1 description as evidence, rerun ticker-value and report whether the values change.

findings.finding: Bear EPS keeps falling after the bear events end. The bear events describe a flat 2027 and a margin reset to 21%; the bear EPS path then declines a further ~5.5-5.8% a year in FY2028-FY2030 (2.78 -> 2.33$) as the margin fades, which is harsher than the events' story but consistent with the margin event. Also the CommScope-dilution and China mechanisms are described but not sized in drivers (no separate revenue or tax line).
findings.fix: Add one bear event or note that the margin glide reaches 21% only by about 2030 (that is what drives the 2028-2030 decline), and size the China exposure (14% of sales, 37% of long-lived assets, tax inquiries 100M + 290M + 60M) as an explicit bear line or state that it is inside the margin reset.

findings.finding: Two scenario events are hypotheses without evidence ids: the bear Kyber architecture change (copper replaced by PCB/co-packaged optics) and the bull AEC share gain after the Credo licence. They are labelled hypothesis, which is correct, but the Kyber one is the central mechanism of the counter-thesis and has no named source.
findings.where: position/core.json scenario_events bear (Kyber) and bull (AEC/Credo); position/field.json
findings.fix: Keep the hypothesis label; if the repair pass retrieves a dated NVIDIA or industry disclosure on Kyber interconnect, attach its id, otherwise list it as a gap in notes.

findings.finding: Expectation gap and red-team: the casefile's red-team verdict is passed with no critical failures (SBC expensed at about 0.41% of revenue, consistent with history). what_must_be_true solves the price at 3.5% average revenue growth over five years versus base 16.9%, but carry-over alone (Q4 2026 at the guide held flat through 2027) already gives about +12% in FY2027, so the low implied growth mainly reflects the engine's 8.6% cost of equity and near-risk-free terminal growth, not a market that expects stagnation. Do not present the 'price assumes 5% growth' row as evidence that the market is pessimistic.
findings.where: casefile.json val.what_must_be_true (growth lever); companies/APH/out/table_he.md row 'מה המחיר של היום מניח'
findings.fix: Add a short behind-the-scenes note that the implied-growth reading is model-dependent (cost of equity 8.59%, terminal growth ~4.5-5.0%) and that the forward P/E at today's price is about 21.7x on base FY2027 EPS, near the own-history median.
